ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic latitude-longitude grid diagram of the western Pacific and part of East Asia, where labels such as 100°E, 120°E, 140°E, 160°E, and 10°N, 20°N, 30°N can be seen; the figure is marked with “western Pacific subtropical high ridge line,” whose position is roughly near 20°N and spans the western Pacific, and there are also labels such as “isobars” nearby. Then reason: the question asks what activity period the ocean surface on the south side of the subtropical high is in. When the subtropical high ridge line moves northward to the latitude shown in the figure, it usually corresponds to the period when the warm sea surface of the northwestern Pacific is active in summer; the northwestern Pacific and the South China Sea area on the south side of the subtropical high have high water temperatures and strong convection, and are the main regions for the generation and development of typhoons. Therefore, the ocean surface on the south side of the subtropical high is in the typhoon activity period.
